name: Quick use notes
description:
Quick use notes

  • Draw until you have all four suits: Spade = place, Heart = actor, Club = pressure, Diamond = leverage. Highest rank sets the main Timer (2–5 () 4, 6–10 () 6, J/Q/K () 8, A () 10).
  • Diamonds are codified outcomes (oaths/rights/tokens) that change position rather than call for a roll.
  • If any A appears, echo stone and spear motifs—cairns that watch, voices that echo, oaths that cut deeper than steel. The ninth stone is warm. The dead are counting.

Additional Features (Cultural Mechanics)

  • Guest-Law: Breaking hospitality stains a name worse than breaking a sword. Guest-right tokens guarantee shelter, but abuse invites a blood feud. A Viterran lord who broke guest-law at Gray Tor had his name struck from the Council's cairn. His own clan disowned him. The cairn has eight names. His is not among them.
  • Wergild System: Every injury has a price in cattle or coin. Wergild keepers maintain reckonings that outlive the injured; weights pass to kin. The lowland courts have no equivalent; they imprison the poor and hang the desperate. The clans consider that barbaric. The clans count in eights. The ninth is the Hollow's.
  • Dwarf Toll Roads: Khaz-Vurim gates charge for passage, but their roads are sure and swift. Pass-rings grant priority, but dwarf law is strict. The Aeler outcasts who run the tolls are exiles—they fled the Deep Vaults because they could not abide the counting. Now they count for the clans, and they are gentle with the weary. They never count to nine.
  • Scottish Folk Horrors (Ubral Bestiary): See the Folk-Horror Bestiary table above for creature mechanics and hooks.
  • Local Patrons (Syncretic Names):
    • The Bone Keeper — Varnek Karn. The chronicler of ancestral wergild; the witness to every blood price. He counts in eights. The ninth is the grave.
    • The Iron Crown — Mykkiel. The law of the lowlands, cold and distant; the clans honor it by breaking it. Its scales have eight weights. The ninth is empty.
    • The Gray Mare — The Traveler. The rider who never tires; the path that leads home through the mist. Her hooves fall in eights. The ninth is a whisper.
    • The Forge Father (Aeler outcast cult) — The Sealed Gate. The fire that shapes iron; the exile who builds a new hearth. He counts his breaths. The ninth is the mountain's.
    • The Cailleach (Winter Hag) — The Pale Shepherd. She who brings the frost and the long dark. Her staff is the ninth branch of the world tree.

Lore Echoes (Cross-Expansion Hooks)

  • The Bitter Root: Daughters of the Cord run a hospice near the Pass of Ashes, tending to the wounded of both sides of the Great Feud. A renegade Sister has hidden a Hollowed in a cairn, trying to settle a blood-weight by feeding the Hollow memories of Viterran tax collectors. The clans do not know whether to thank her or burn her. The cairn now has eight stones. The ninth is her name.
  • Malachai, the Chained Angel: A silver coin that never spends appears in the palm of every third corpse pulled from a hill-fall. Take it, and the dead will give you their last breath—but the coin will taste of peat smoke and regret. The coin has eight edges. The ninth is a scar.
  • The Gray Wanderer's Grimoire: Ubral psions are called “Stone-Listeners.” They press their foreheads to cairns and hear the names of everyone who has touched that stone. The Lady of Tor employs three; they have not spoken aloud in a decade. They count in eights. The ninth name is always theirs.
  • The Threshold Compendium: The Pass of Ashes is a Class II Anchor—the spirits of Viterran knights who froze to death in a blizzard still march there, looking for a way home. Saikou Ira left a silver mirror at the summit. The mirror shows the knights their own corpses. They have not advanced since. The mirror has eight sides. The ninth is a crack.

Ubral Superstitions (burn for +1 die once)

  • Bread to the Cairn: Crumble a crust at the base of a standing stone. Ignore the first Upland Mist penalty. `[SUPERSTITION]`
  • Knot the Guest-Cup: Tie a single knot in the handle of a drinking cup. Cancel Feud Rekindled or take (-1) die on your next hospitality roll (your choice). `[SUPERSTITION]`
  • Name to the Ford: Whisper a dead enemy's name into the Wergild Ford. Gain +1 Effect when claiming redress from their kin this scene, but mark Obligation to the Lady of Tor. `[SUPERSTITION]`
  • Count the Eighth: Before entering a cairn's shadow, count your breaths to eight. Stop. If you reach nine, the cairn will count you. `[SUPERSTITION]`
  • Iron to the Kelpie: Drop a cold iron nail into a loch before crossing. The water horse will not trouble you for one crossing. `[SUPERSTITION]`

Thematic SB Spend Table

Minor Complications (1 SB)

  • Exposure: Your actions draw unwanted attention from clan guards or reiver scouts.
  • Noise: Sounds of your actions alert nearby watch-fires or hill guides.
  • Trace: Evidence of your passage marks your route for trackers or feud-kin.
  • Delay: A brief but meaningful setback costs you time or favorable weather.
  • Supply Strain: Mark +1 segment on a relevant resource timer.

Moderate Setbacks (2 SB)

  • Alarm Raised: Hill guide or clan chief becomes aware and begins responding.
  • Position Lost: You lose advantageous ground/cover/stealth due to mist or bridge collapse.
  • Foe Appears: A reiver band or feud-kin arrives on scene.
  • Gear Trouble: A piece of equipment becomes Compromised/Neglected.
  • Lock/Barrier: A simple obstacle now requires a test to overcome.

Serious Trouble (3 SB)

  • Reinforcements: Additional clan warriors, reivers, or dwarf wardens arrive.
  • Key Gear Breaks: A crucial tool/weapon becomes temporarily unusable.
  • Major Twist: The situation fundamentally changes—feud declared/bridge falls/snow closes pass.
  • Rail Tick: Advance a relevant campaign/front timer by 1 segment.
  • Condition Applied: Mark Fatigue 1/Harm 1/Condition appropriate to fiction.

Major Turns (4+ SB)

  • Trap Springs: A prepared danger activates with full effect.
  • Authority Arrival: Lady of Tor, Council of Cairns, or Stone-Speaker intervenes.
  • Scene Shift: The environment changes dramatically—mist thickens/bridge drops/hill falls.
  • Patron Omen: Divine/arcane forces take notice—omen appears/blessing lost/curse manifests.
  • Narrative Pivot: The story takes an unexpected turn that reframes objectives.

Region-Specific SB Options

  • Ubral (Stone & Oath): Cairns shift position, voices echo from empty air, oaths bind mid-speech. The ninth stone glows.
  • Ubral (Hill Law): Paths reroute without warning, tolls increase mid-journey, guest-rights expire. The eighth cup is the last.
  • Ubral (Feud Culture): Insults are overheard, weapons appear in sheaths, kin arrive unsummoned. The dead are watching.

Pursuit Ladder (Near / Mid / Far)

  • Advance/Withdraw (Wits + Navigation): On a hit, shift one band. On a strong hit, also impose Bog Mist.
  • Cut the Bridge (Presence + Command): On a hit, freeze range for one exchange; if a Pass-Ring is in your possession, +1 die.
  • Weather the Squall (Endurance + Survival): On a hit in Snow-Squall, you pick who finds shelter; on a miss, the GM does.

Boss Seeds (Stone & Spear)

  • The Wolf-Road Captain (reiver-king on a piebald mare) — Phases: Ride-Through () Torch the Fold () Laugh in Rain. Cracks: present a Watch-Code or Guide's Braid to reduce his effect; strike a truce with a season's cattle. He counts his victims in eights. The ninth is himself.
  • The Bride-Thief of Black Broom (mask of bog-rush) — Phases: Switch the Bride () Bog Embrace () Nettle Oath. Cracks: play a Bride-Charter to freeze blades; a Well-Blessing nulls one bog move. She has stolen eight brides. The ninth stole her.
  • Stone Warden of Khaz-Vurim (Aeler outcast toll-magistrate) — Phases: Double the Toll () Weigh the Lie () Seal the Switchback. Cracks: present two of Pass-Ring, Stamped Load-List, Named Sponsor to downgrade his authority. He counts in eights. Do not let him reach nine.
  • The Oath-Eater Wight (cairn-bound revenant) — Phases: Take the Word () Cold of Cairn () Bind Witness. Cracks: Oath-Bracelet or a skald's stanza spoken over bread and blood cancels one move; settle an ancestral wergild. It was betrayed on the ninth oath. It will not forgive.
  • Gray-Tor Hedge-Witch (heather crown, ash staff) — Phases: Weather-Turn () Hag-Stone Sight () Bind the Gate. Cracks: gift a Bloom Allotment or a winter's salt; a Council Audience compels parley. She speaks in eights. The ninth word is a curse.
  • The Each Uisge (Lord of the Loch) — Phases: Beckoning () The Ride () The Drowning. Cracks: offer a cold iron bridle, speak its true name (carved on a stone at the bottom of the loch), or sacrifice a horse in your place.

Legendary Sites & Trials

  • Sheepwalk Ledge Trial — Speak one honest lie to pass. On success, set Position one step safer for the next border scene; on failure, start Kin Arrive. The ledge has eight steps. The ninth is a story.
  • Wergild Ford Weighing — Cast silver on the table-rock. If paid in full, clear 1 Feud-Smoke; if short, Wergild Breach enters play. The rock has eight weights. The ninth is a ghost.
  • Pass of Ashes Vigil — Hold a fire through the night storm. Success grants Shelter Writ; a miss summons the Oath-Eater Wight at weak strength. The fire must be fed eight times. The ninth feeding is your memory.

Extensions (Plug-in)

  • Oath Dial (Honor () Cunning): Track the party's footing between honor and pragmatism.
    • Honor High: +1 Position when invoking guest-right, keeping truce, or paying wergild promptly; first ambush/raid action each session starts one step worse.
    • Cunning High: +1 Effect on raids, evasions, and border tricks; first formal parley or oath-bound request each session starts one step worse.
    • Center the dial by restoring stolen cattle, hosting an enemy well, or submitting to a cairn ruling. The dial has eight positions. The ninth is a truce.
  • Feud Math (fast settlement): Lay three markers: Blood, Beasts, Blame.
    1. Make a single Parley/Command/Study roll per side. On a hit, move one marker to your side; great Effect moves two.
    2. Win any two to settle: Blood = oath/hostage, Beasts = wergild in cattle/coin, Blame = public apology/verse.
    3. Miss: mark Feud-Smoke [4]. At 4, the losing side names a lawful target (bridge, herd, guide). The target has eight days to pay. The ninth is the Hollow's.
  • Guest-Right Procedure:
    • Present a Guest-Token (or bread and salt). Host must choose: Shelter, Escort at Dawn, or Neutral Meal.
    • Breaking it creates Blood-Oath [6] against the violator; any Ubral ally may spend 1 () to tick it twice.
    • Abiding it clears 1 tick from Feud-Smoke and grants +1d to the next social action in that steading. The oath is witnessed by the hearth. The hearth counts in eights.
  • Watchfire Net (ridge signals):
    • Two timers: Beat the Beacons vs Ridge Aflame (size by highest rank in your seed).
    • Choose a lane each exchange: Low Fold (slow, stealth), Sheepwalk (tricky, quick), Road (fast, obvious).
    • Advantage: Low Fold(,,)Road (conceal), Road(,,)Sheepwalk (speed), Sheepwalk(,,)Low Fold (shortcuts).
    • False Alarm (1 SB): light or douse a misleading brazier; shift one segment between the two timers. The beacons have eight signals. The ninth is war.
  • Reiver Ride (mounted chase):
    • Track Remounts (3): each push for speed trades 1 remount for +1d or +1 Effect. At 0, gain Blown Mounts condition.
    • Hag-Stone Cut: pass a known gap (Sheepwalk Ledge, Droppers' Bridge) to force pursuers to roll or fall behind.
    • The reivers ride in eights. The ninth horse is a lie.
  • Khaz-Vurim Protocol (Aeler Outcast Rules):
    • Present any two: Pass-Ring, Stamped Load-List, Named Sponsor. Two = safe passage; one = pay toll + scrutiny; none = delay and search.
    • Stone-Clause may override one dwarf law once; afterwards start Marked Notice [3] with the wardens (prices rise, patience falls).
    • Measured Truth: you may substitute exact weights/measures for charm or coin to improve Position by one step with dwarves.
    • Aeler outcast smiths accept stories as payment for small repairs—the story must be about a betrayal. They are collecting evidence for a case they will never bring. They count their breaths. The ninth is the mountain's.
  • Bride-Peace Interlude:
    • Play a Bride-Charter to suspend violence at a scene. Everyone sheaths—or earns Song Shame [4]. When it fills, a skald memorializes the insult (ongoing -1d with that clan).
    • The bride has eight ribbons. The ninth is a knife.
  • Start-of-Scene Omens (1d6):
    1. Clear Ridge: first signal test gains +1d.
    2. Lowing Herd: +1d to tracking or herding; -1d to stealth near cattle.
    3. Wet Stone: climbs start one step worse; mending gear is easier (free repair tick).
    4. Old Verse Remembered: first oath/plea gains +1d if spoken in rhyme.
    5. Border Drums: Viterra patrols near; papers safer, raiding harsher.
    6. Dwarf Toll Day: prices firm; any () tied to roads counts double value at the Steps.
  • Plug-in SB Conversions (Ubral Flavor):
    • 1 SB () Mud and Heather: footing worsens; next physical action (-1)d or mark Winded.
    • 2 SB () Kin Arrive: add a rival cousin/ally who changes the ask or splits the pot.
    • 3+ SB () Cairn Decrees: a standing stone “speaks” (witnesses recall the law); swap one held () for a lesser right until you make amends. The stone speaks in eights. The ninth word is your name.
  • Reputation Echoes:
    • Guest-Faithful: once/session downgrade a social backlash inside a steading; next time you refuse hospitality, mark Feud-Smoke +1.
    • Reiver-Favored: +1 Effect to seize cattle/contraband on the move; city gates start one step worse Position.
    • Stone-Friend: +1d with dwarf wardens on roads; any false measure triggers Marked Notice +1.
Patronage & Power

In Ubral, power flows through clan bonds, guest-right, and the careful balance of honor and iron. Clan chiefs maintain authority through wergild, moots, and the respect of their people, while the Aeler outcasts of Khaz-Vurim wield influence through their control of mountain passes and forges. Law is personal and passed down through generations, with each oath and weight creating a web of obligation that can last centuries. The Viterran crown claims suzerainty; the clans call that claim “the ink of thieves.”

But older powers stir in the glens and lochs. The cailleach watches from the high corries, and the each uisge waits beneath the black water. The clans do not fight these spirits; they propitiate them with offerings of iron, salt, and silence. A chief who forgets the old ways may find his cattle drowned and his children cursed.

For the GM:

Patronage in Ubral revolves around hospitality, protection, and the resolution of feuds. Rewards often take the form of tokens, charters, or safe passage that can be leveraged into greater influence. To emphasize this, use the faction timers, let rival clans issue conflicting protections, and remember the Aeler outcasts—they are exiles, not tourists. They will help a clan for a story, but they will never forget a slight. They count in eights. Do not let them reach nine.

In Ubral, your word is your bond, and your bond determines whether you walk in peace or peril. The lowlands write their laws in ink; Ubral carves them in stone. The ink fades. The stone remembers. And the dead are always counting.
